q: Why do you need a common bottom to work out 1/3 + 1/4?
o: Because the rule says to multiply the bottoms
Thirds and quarters are different-sized pieces, and you can only count pieces of the same size
why: Turn both into twelfths: 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12. Then you are counting pieces of the same size.
You may split the TOP of a fraction: a/a + b/a = 1 + b/a.
Only when a = 0. Try 1/(1 + 1) = 1/2, but 1/1 + 1/1 = 2. You can split a fraction's top, never its bottom.
Dividing by 4 means multiplying by 1/4: 2/3 × 1/4 = 2/12 = 1/6. Sharing 2/3 between 4 should give less, not more.

q: A fraction with a bigger bottom is always smaller.
why: Myth. That's only true when the tops are equal. 3/8 = 0.375 is bigger than 1/4 = 0.25.
